$comment: The components every CoolMS UI kit provides, by name, and the states each must render. A kit declares which of its components implements each entry (kit.contract.json); tools/check-kit.mjs fails when one is missing, or a state is. Names follow ui-angular's where it has one.

button.purpose: An action. Primary, secondary, danger; an icon may lead.
button.notes: locked = allowed once elevated (the server answered `elevate`): drawn with a lock, choosing it asks for elevation. In a client that never elevates an `elevate` answer is not offered at all. Height: --cms-control-height-md (sm in a dense row, lg standing alone), 44px on a touch screen; never a spacing token.

text-field.purpose: One line of text, with a label, help and an error.
text-field.notes: pinned = set by the environment and not editable here; the help names what pins it. Height: --cms-control-height-md (sm in a dense row, lg standing alone), 44px on a touch screen; never a spacing token.

select.purpose: One choice from a list, with a label, help and an error.
select.notes: Height: --cms-control-height-md (sm in a dense row, lg standing alone), 44px on a touch screen; never a spacing token.

toggle.purpose: On or off, with a label on the same baseline.

modal.purpose: A dialog over the page; Escape and the scrim close it unless it holds unsaved work.

confirm-dialog.purpose: A question before a destructive or irreversible action; the labels name the outcomes.

toast.purpose: A short, transient report of what happened.

loading.purpose: Something is being read; says what.
loading.notes: Superseded by state; leaves the contract once every kit implements state.

empty-state.purpose: Nothing to show, and why; optionally what to do.
empty-state.notes: Superseded by state; leaves the contract once every kit implements state.

error-banner.purpose: A read failed; says why, offers retry when retrying can help.

page-header.purpose: The page's title, its scope line and its actions.

tab-strip.purpose: Sections of one object, one at a time.

list.purpose: Rows of objects, each opened by a press; a row's other actions in its menu.

parts.row: One anatomy for every list on a phone screen: a leading icon or avatar (40px); a title, one line, --cms-font-size-body, semibold while unread; a secondary line, one line, --cms-font-size-meta, --cms-text-muted; trailing meta, the time or date with a count badge under it. Rows sit on one surface (--cms-surface), separated by --cms-border-light, padded --cms-space-3 --cms-space-4; no bordered cards and no list inside a card.
parts.density: Every list's row height comes from the list density tokens, the same in every list (Mail, Chat, Drive and the rest), and in no list from its own padding: from tablet width up --cms-list-row-height (one line, 40px) and --cms-list-row-height-two-line (a title and a secondary line, 52px); at phone width --cms-list-row-height-phone (48px) and --cms-list-row-height-phone-two-line (60px). The mail list is three lines at every width (the sender and the date; the subject; the preview) at --cms-list-row-height-three-line (84px); the compact one- and two-line heights are for the other lists, Drive's among them. Each is the row's least height, its content centred in it; a row whose text wraps grows. At phone width the whole row is the touch target, and every control in it (a checkbox, a star, a menu button) is at least --cms-touch-target-min (44px).
parts.columns: A list whose rows show the same fields side by side, from tablet width up. Header row: one line, the column names in the list's meta text, kept in sight at the top while the list scrolls; not a control (no sorting yet). Columns in the host's order. The first is the name column: the lead icon and the name; it takes the width left and is the only one that truncates, with an ellipsis and the full name as its title. The others keep their own content width and never wrap. Alignment: a number (a size, a count) at the end; a date, a time or a name at the start; the header cell aligned as its column. A row with no value in a column shows nothing there, never a dash or "unknown". A column the server does not serve for any row is not drawn at all. Height: --cms-list-row-height (one line). The whole row is one control: it opens what it names; Enter opens the focused row. Below tablet width there are no columns: the row is two lines, the name as its first and the other columns' values joined by " · " as its second (--cms-list-row-height-phone-two-line).
parts.selection: A list whose rows can be checked (Mail's, Drive's) selects as a desktop file list does, the same in every host. Click: opens the row, clears every check, and makes it the anchor. Ctrl/Cmd+click: toggles the row's check without opening it; it becomes the anchor. Shift+click, on the row or its checkbox: checks the range from the anchor to that row; the anchor stays, so a second Shift+click re-spans from it. Up/Down: moves the focus, and the focused row opens as a click would, checks unchanged; while two or more rows are checked it moves the focus only, and the reading pane keeps the count. Shift+Up/Down: moves the focus one row and checks the range from the anchor to it (going back shrinks the range). Space: toggles the focused row's check; it becomes the anchor. Ctrl/Cmd+A, while the list has the focus: checks every loaded row (never the rows not loaded); elsewhere the browser's own. Esc: clears the checks; with none checked it does what it did before (closing a view or a menu). A row that cannot be acted on (Mail's rows read from the server, not stored) has no checkbox, is never checked, and is skipped by a range and by Ctrl/Cmd+A. The actions bar acts on every checked row from one; from two checked rows the reading pane shows the count ("N selected", in the interface's words) in place of a message. Each checked row's state is its checkbox's (checked), and the count is a status line read out when it changes. aria-multiselectable and aria-selected belong to a list drawn as a listbox or a grid; a list of rows each holding a button and a checkbox has neither, its checkboxes say it.

list.notes: pulled = the list is being pulled from its top to refresh it (screen-shell, pull).

avatar.purpose: A person or an account, by picture or initials.
avatar.notes: presence and connection are a dot at the avatar's bottom right. On the person's own avatar in a bar it is the live connection: --cms-success connected, --cms-warning reconnecting, --cms-text-muted offline; a press or tap says which, in words. On other people it is their presence where the server declares it (chat members), and none where it does not (mail senders). deleted = a person whose account is gone: a neutral person icon on --cms-surface-muted, never initials of the stored name. Initials leave out a trailing lowercase " via <service>" and take each word's first letter or digit.

elevation-required.purpose: Says that an action needs elevation, and offers it (theme-admin); never shown in a client that does not elevate.
elevation-required.notes: Superseded by state; leaves the contract once every kit implements state.

context-menu.purpose: The selected object's actions, exactly the action bar's for it; only on the client's own objects.
behaviour: Disabled item: an action the server says cannot run now, for a reason it names, stays in the menu as a menuitem with aria-disabled="true", reached by the arrow keys, its reason shown beside or under its label and named by aria-describedby; choosing it shows the reason and does nothing else, and the menu stays open. The rule is the pane toolbar's Disabled rule.

state.purpose: One component for every state a page, a card or a line of text can be in instead of its content: being read, nothing to show, a read that failed, a refusal, or an elevation the content needs. The same API and the same look in every kit, from the tokens.

api.title: string: what the state is, in the caller's words
api.description: string, optional: why, or what to do
api.icon: string, optional, the empty kind only: an icon name from contract/icons.json, drawn above the title in the state's text colour, decorative
api.action: optional: a label and a handler -- Retry for an error, or what an empty state suggests; for elevation-required the kit's own Elevate, the same flow the error banner offers. denied never offers an action: a refusal is the server's last word, and a retry or a request would only be refused again
api.placement: page (centred in the content area) | block (centred in its card) | inline (small, beside text)

behaviour: loading shows nothing at all -- neither spinner nor title -- until state-delay (300ms), then both together, so a read that answers sooner shows nothing; the spinner is drawn, never a glyph. A kit may have its title announced to assistive technology from the start, visually hidden until the delay

role="status" with aria-live="polite" on every kind. Every kind shows the caller's title and description as given, and adds no words of its own beyond its action's label (for elevation-required: Elevate, and the line saying elevation is not available here)
the spinner is spinner-color on spinner-track, spinner-size-<placement>, one turn per spinner-duration; with prefers-reduced-motion it pulses instead of turning
elevation-required is not offered by a kit whose clients never elevate (notOffered, with the reason)

Whose words a refusal or a failure says, in every host and every component. The line is whether the server declared the problem, not the status class: a problem response with a declared type (any type but about:blank) carries a detail written for the person, and the host says that detail as given, whatever the status -- a refused action (4xx), a validation refusal, and a declared failure such as a mail provider's refusal of a send (502) alike; its type is for behaviour only (an icon, a link to the fix, a retry, tests), never to replace or rewrite the text, and there is no host wording per type. A validation refusal (422 with violations) says each field's message as given, next to its field (outside a form, the first one), whether or not its type is declared; its top-level detail is not shown. An undeclared fault (type about:blank, or no problem body) and a network failure say the host's own one generic sentence, "Something went wrong. Try again.", never any text of theirs, which may carry internals. A declared problem with no detail (an older server) says the one generic "Not available right now". A detail is always drawn as plain text, never as HTML. The same holds for an action's disabled reason (pane-toolbar, Disabled)
state.notes: Supersedes loading, empty-state and elevation-required: those three stay in the contract until every kit implements state, then leave it in the next contract version. error-banner stays: a failed read above content that is still shown.

parts.empty pane: A pane with nothing to show (Mail's reading pane with no message open, Chat's conversation pane with no conversation open, a Drive folder with nothing in it) is never left blank: it draws the state component, kind empty, placement page, centred in the pane, from the node the server declares for it in the page's tree. The node's label is the title, its description the description, its icon the icon, and its action, where the tree gives one and its condition holds (Chat's New chat, Drive's Upload), the one action, run as the same action elsewhere on the page. The host adds no words of its own, and until the node is served it keeps the words it had. From tablet width up only: at phone width a pane with nothing in it is not shown, the list stands in its place.

file-viewer.purpose: One way to look at a file: over the page, with the same parts, states and keys whatever the file is and whichever kit draws it. What draws the file itself is an adapter chosen by its content type, so a new type adds an adapter and not a viewer.

api.file: name, content type, size, and the addresses to read it inline, to download it and to view it as a page (/view/<id>), all as the server gave them
api.canEdit: boolean, from the server's answer about this file for this person: its write permission. A kit never works it out from a role, an owner or a path
api.onEdit: optional: the existing editor component for this type, hosted in the content for the editing state; the viewer embeds no editor of its own. With canEdit false, or with none, no Edit is drawn at all
api.siblings: optional: the files around this one, in the caller's order, for previous and next, and for the strip when they are a set, such as a message's attachments
api.onClose: handler. The caller decides what closing means for its address

parts.overlay: Dark, whatever the scheme, covering the page and holding everything below. The page behind cannot be reached or scrolled while it is open
parts.top bar: At the left: Close, the file type's badge, the file's name (truncated, with the whole name available), and its position in its set ("2 of 17") where it has one. At the right, in this order: Download, Print (where the adapter can print), Open separately, then Edit, the one amber button, only with canEdit. While editing, the save status and Done take the actions' place. An adapter adds nothing here. A kit may add Fullscreen as an extra, as one more icon before Download
parts.viewer bar: Along the foot, centred: what this content type needs, from its adapter: previous, page and next, zoom out, zoom in, and Fit width and Fit page. It says "Preview not available" under no-preview. It never holds a file action
parts.content: The adapter, filling what is left. It scrolls inside itself, and the overlay never scrolls as a document
parts.thumbnails: For a paged file at a wide width: a rail of its pages at the left, numbered, with the current one marked. Not drawn on a phone
parts.siblings: Previous and next at the content's edges, for the other files of its set, each hidden at its end of the list
parts.attachment strip: For a set of files, such as a message's attachments: along the foot, above the viewer bar, at a wide width, each with its type badge and name, and the current one marked. Not drawn on a phone

adapters.rule: Chosen by the server's content type, never by the file's name. A type no adapter claims is no-preview. A kit declares the adapters it has; one it lacks is no-preview there, not an error
adapters.application/pdf: paged: drawn in a sandboxed frame that holds no credential and can reach nothing
adapters.image/svg+xml: picture, only as an image element or rasterised, never inlined, since an SVG can hold a script
adapters.application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedoc: document: paged where the format has pages
sheet: read-only here; Edit goes to the editor
presentation: paged, one slide to a page, read-only here
adapters.text/* except text/html, and JSON: text: escaped, in a monospaced block, with a size limit past which it is no-preview
adapters.audio/*, video/*: media: the platform's player, with no autoplay
adapters.text/html and anything else: no-preview. A page is never rendered as a page here

behaviour: The states are the state component's, in placement page, inside the content: loading while the file is read; error with the caller's words and Retry when the read failed, or no Retry when the server says the file is gone or refused; no-preview, its kind empty, with Download as its action. The top bar stays in all three, so Close and Download are always there
Download offers the server's download address, whatever the adapter. A person without the right to read the file never reaches the viewer: a refusal on opening is the caller's
Edit is drawn only with the server's write permission, and is absent rather than disabled without it

Editing is a state of the viewer, without leaving the page: the content hosts the existing editor component for the type (document, sheet, image), and the viewer has no editor of its own. The top bar shows the save status and Done. There are two exits: Done returns to viewing, and Close leaves the whole viewer, asking first with unsaved changes. That question, the editing-closing state, is reached by Close alone. The address carries the state (/view/<id>?edit), so a reload keeps it
If the file changed elsewhere meanwhile, the viewer warns and offers the newer version; it never overwrites silently, as with drafts. That is the editing-conflict state
Open separately opens /view/<id> as a page, never the raw file. Print is offered where the adapter can print: a PDF, a paged document, a sheet

Focus moves into the overlay on opening, onto Close unless the adapter takes it, is held inside while open, and returns to what opened it on closing. role="dialog", aria-modal="true", labelled by the file's name

Keys: Escape closes the overlay only while viewing. While editing it belongs to the editor (its menus, its selection) and never closes the overlay. Left and Right are previous and next, only when focus is not in something that uses them, such as a text field or an adapter's own scroll. Plus, minus and 0 are zoom in, out and reset where the adapter has zoom. Every action can be reached by Tab, and has a visible focus and an accessible name, icon or not
A change to the next file moves the address where the caller keeps one, and announces the new name politely

Phone, below breakpoint-md: the overlay takes the whole screen. The top bar stays on one line: Close, the badge, the name giving way first, then Edit as an amber icon where it is offered, and a menu behind ... holding every other action. Position dots above the viewer bar show the place in a set. No thumbnails and no attachment strip. The viewer bar stays, condensed to icons. Each target is at least touch-target-min; a swipe is previous and next only where the adapter has not taken the gesture, and pinch is the adapter's
prefers-reduced-motion: no animation between files
file-viewer.notes: Follows the approved mockups. Replaces the admin's separate viewers once ui-angular implements it, one viewer per step: document-viewer-angular as the adapter host, Word first; pdf-angular as the PDF adapter, keeping the sandboxed frame's guarantees; image preview in the file manager and media library; the sheet read-only view. No release of this contract until ui-react and ui-angular both implement it, as with state.

file-picker.purpose: One way to choose files that already exist in the person's spaces, such as Drive, to attach or use elsewhere without downloading them and uploading them again. The kit knows no API: the host gives the spaces, lists folders, and receives the chosen entries.

api.spaces: the spaces the person may read, each with an id and a name to show, in the host's order. With one, no space switch is drawn
api.list: list(space, path, cursor?) returns { entries, next? }: one page of a folder, in the host's order (folders first is the stated default), and next when more follow. Each entry has id, name, kind (folder or file), size and mimeType for a file. A refusal the host reports as denied, a failure as error
api.disabledReason: optional: disabledReason(entry) returns the host's own reason a file cannot be chosen (not readable, a type it will not send), or nothing. The kit shows the reason and never ticks such a file
api.budget: optional: { usedBytes, limitBytes, cost? }, what the host has spent of a limit before this choice, such as a message's size against its mailbox's limit. cost(entry) is what a file adds against that limit, the file's size when not given; a host whose limit counts something else, such as an encoded message, says so through cost. The kit computes what is left after the selection, and the files that would go over it
api.confirmLabel: the confirm action's words for a count, by key, such as "Attach {count} files"
api.onConfirm: handler, given the chosen entries: id, name, size, mimeType, and the space and path each was chosen in, so the host needs no second lookup

parts.dialog: Over the page, labelled by its title. Desktop: a dialog of fixed height whose list scrolls inside it. Phone: the whole screen
parts.space switch: At the top, when there is more than one space: the space shown, and the others to switch to. Switching keeps the selection
parts.breadcrumb: A navigation landmark: the space, then each folder down to the one shown, each a way back to it, and Up
parts.list: The folder's entries: a folder opens, a file ticks. Each row shows its kind's icon, name, and a file's size. A disabled file shows its reason and cannot be ticked
parts.selection chip: "{count} selected", when anything is: it opens the list of everything chosen, across folders, each with a way to remove it, and Clear
parts.footer: The whole selection's count and total size; with a budget, "{left} of {limit} left after these"; Cancel, and the confirm action, whose label carries the count. On a phone the footer stays at the foot while the list scrolls

behaviour: The selection is the person's across folders and spaces: what is ticked in one folder stays ticked after going elsewhere and coming back, and the footer and chip count all of it, not this folder's alone

With a budget, a file that would take the selection over what is left is disabled with that reason, and over-budget is the state when the selection already does. This is computed in the kit from the budget and the selection, so every host behaves alike. The host's own disabledReason is shown first where both apply
The confirm action is disabled with nothing chosen, and while over the budget
Paging: when list gives next, the kit asks for the following page as the list nears its end, keeping what is shown; paging is the state while it does

States are the state component's, in placement block, inside the list: loading while a folder is read; empty for a folder with nothing in it; error with the host's words and Retry; denied for a folder the person may not open, shown in place, with no action, and the dialog stays open so another folder can be chosen

Keys: the list is a listbox with aria-multiselectable. Up and Down move, Enter opens a folder, Space ticks a file, Backspace goes Up a folder, and Escape cancels. The breadcrumb is a nav. Every action can be reached by Tab, and has a visible focus and an accessible name
Focus moves into the dialog on opening, onto the list, is held inside while open, and returns to what opened it on closing. role="dialog", aria-modal="true"
Strings are the host's catalogue's, by key, with the counts and sizes formatted for the person's language
Phone, below breakpoint-md: the whole screen, the footer sticky at the foot, each target at least touch-target-min
file-picker.notes: First used by compose's From Drive; the admin implements the same entry in Angular, on its tree picker where it fits. No release of this contract until ui-react and ui-angular both implement it, as with file-viewer.

pane-toolbar.purpose: The one row of actions at the top of a pane, drawn the same way in every kit and every host: the same height in every pane of a screen, so the rows line up across it, and one way of giving way when the pane narrows. Which actions it holds, in which groups and order, with which icons, and which of them are danger, may go behind More actions or never do, are the server's, as the nodes of a NaviGraph tree; the row draws what it is given.

api.label: string: the toolbar's accessible name, in the host's words, such as "Message actions"
api.actions: { id, label, icon, group, overflow?, danger?, disabled?, reason?, busy? }[]: the server's action nodes for which the host has a handler, in the tree's order. label is the accessible name always, and the tooltip once labels hide. group: groups follow the order of their first action, and a separator is drawn between two. overflow: a number; the lowest hides its label first and, once every label is hidden, goes behind More actions first, and actions sharing a number go together, such as a toggle's two states; an action with no number keeps its label longest and goes behind More actions only in a row too narrow to hold it once every numbered action has gone, so that nothing is cut off. overflow 0 means menu only: the action is never drawn in the row, only behind More actions, at any width, and its label is not part of the row's giving way. reason: why a disabled action is disabled, the server's sentence as given; shown on hover, focus and a press and named by aria-describedby
api.status: optional: the trailing status slot's text, such as "Synced at 14:32", formatted by the host for the person's language
api.moreLabel: More actions' accessible name and tooltip, from the host's catalogue: "More actions" in English
api.action: emitted with the chosen action's id. The row knows nothing of what an action does

parts.row: Exactly pane-toolbar-height tall at the very top of its pane, on one line that never wraps and never scrolls: the actions at the start, the status slot at the end, everything centred vertically in it
parts.action: A button with its icon, then its label. Actions sit space-1 apart. In a web kit, an action whose label is hidden carries cms-pane-toolbar__action--bare, and an action drawn without an icon (a name the table lacks) carries cms-pane-toolbar__action--text; the row carries cms-pane-toolbar--labels-partly-hidden or cms-pane-toolbar--labels-hidden as its state
parts.separator: Between two groups: a vertical line in border, role="separator" with aria-orientation="vertical", never focused. Drawn only between two groups that both still show something in the row
parts.more: The More actions button (...), after the last action shown, drawn only while at least one action is behind it: a menu button that opens the kit's context-menu, listing those actions
parts.status slot: At the end of the row: text, not an action, in text-muted at font-size-meta. It takes the width the actions leave and truncates with an ellipsis, its whole text kept as its title
parts.header row: From tablet width up a screen of columns has two rows that line up across it. The first is the toolbar row, --cms-pane-toolbar-height: in Mail, Compose at the top of the side column, the list's bar (Refresh and when it was synced) and the open message's actions. The second is the header row, --cms-pane-header-height: in Mail, the mailbox card in the side column and the list's title with its filters. Each row is that height exactly in every column, its content centred in it, so the bottom borders of each row are one line across the screen; a column with nothing for a row keeps the row, empty. What a row holds stays on one line: the list's filters never wrap, they scroll sideways within the row where the column is too narrow; and a note that belongs to the row's content (the mailbox card's connection line, a status) goes under the row, not in it, so the row stays its height. Below breakpoint-tablet one column shows at a time and the rows are the screen shell's.

behaviour: Alignment: every pane of a screen starts at the same top and draws its row there, at pane-toolbar-height, so the rows line up across the screen. A pane with nothing to act on keeps its row, empty, at that height. The side column beside the panes starts at that top too: its first element aligns its top edge with the rows, and an element that is one control takes pane-toolbar-height exactly, the control centred in it

The row is measured on its own width as its pane resizes, never on the window's: panes split and resize independently, and a breakpoint of the window would fight them. In a web kit, a ResizeObserver on the row

Giving way, in this order as the row narrows: (1) every action shows its icon and its label; (2) when they no longer fit, labels hide one by one in the order actions would go behind More actions: by overflow number, the lowest first and those sharing a number together, the fewest that let the row fit; actions with no overflow number hide theirs last, from the end of the row back; (3) only once every label is hidden and the icons still do not fit, actions go behind More actions by their overflow number, the lowest first and those sharing a number together, the fewest that let the rest and More actions fit. More actions takes an icon's width itself, so one action alone goes behind it only when that alone saves room (an action wider than an icon, such as one that keeps its label) and no other could go with it: a menu of one icon saves none. Menu-only actions (overflow 0) are behind it always, so More actions is drawn whenever one is shown, even alone; the rule that one action never goes behind it alone counts only the actions that could have stayed in the row. (4) Only where the row still cannot hold the rest and More actions once every numbered action has gone, the actions with no overflow number go behind it too, one by one from the end of the row back, the fewest that let the rest and More actions fit: no action is ever cut off at the row's edge, and More actions is always reached. They are listed after the numbered ones, in the row's order. As the row widens, everything comes back in the reverse order: actions from behind More actions first, then labels, the last hidden first
Giving way never reorders the row: the actions still shown keep their places. More actions lists the actions behind it by their overflow number, each with its icon and its label, as in the row
The host passes only the actions it has a handler for: a node it cannot run is left out, the rest keep their order and groups, and a group left empty is not drawn, nor is its separator

Icons: a node's icon is a Bootstrap Icons name. Each kit holds one table from those names to its own icons. A name the table lacks shows the action's label alone, with no empty icon box and no stand-in glyph, also while the other actions hide their labels, and the row measures it that way: its label is its width with labels hidden too. Behind More actions it is listed without an icon

A hidden label: an action whose label is hidden shows it as a tooltip on hover and on keyboard focus, kept while the pointer is over it and dismissed with Escape, and its accessible name stays the label: a tooltip is never the only name. A toggle names its next state by its label (two nodes sharing an overflow number), so its name always says what choosing it does

Danger: an action whose node says danger is drawn as the button's danger state, its icon and label in danger, and as the context-menu's item-danger when it is behind More actions. No other action is drawn as danger

Disabled: an action the server says cannot run now, for a reason it names, is drawn disabled, never left out: aria-disabled="true" (never the disabled attribute), kept in the row's focus order and in More actions when it has overflowed, with its reason. The reason is the server's sentence for it, shown as given: the server owns an action and its state, and the reason is part of that state, so the admin, the web and the app say one wording, translated on the server alone, and a new reason needs no host release. The node also carries the reason's code, for behaviour only (an icon, a link to how to fix it, tests), never to replace or rewrite the sentence; a host that needs another form, such as a shorter one, asks for a server-side variant and writes no wording of its own. Only while a node gives no sentence (an older server) does a host show one generic "Not available right now", never wording per code. It shows on hover, on focus and on a press, as text the action names with aria-describedby (not only a title), so it is reached and announced without a pointer. A press, Enter or Space shows the reason and does nothing else: no request, no notice, no change. An action absent from the tree, or one whose condition hides it, stays absent; only one that says why it cannot run is drawn disabled. The same holds in every place an action is offered: the row's context menu and the checked-rows bar

Busy: an action whose work is under way shows a spinner in its icon's place, spinner-size-inline, after state-delay, so a quick one shows nothing; it is aria-busy="true", keeps its label and name, and a second press does not run it again

Keys: role="toolbar" with the host's label, and one Tab stop: Tab enters on the action focused last, the first at the start; Left and Right move between the actions shown and More actions, without wrapping; Home and End go to the first and the last. Disabled actions are reached; separators and the status slot are not

More actions: aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded, named by moreLabel. Enter, Space or Down opens the menu on its first item, Up on its last; Up and Down move in it; Escape closes it and returns focus to More actions; Tab closes it

At tablet and phone widths, below breakpoint-desktop, each action is at least touch-target-min square, and the row stays pane-toolbar-height with space-1 above and below it. Below breakpoint-tablet one pane shows at a time; the rules are the same, measured on the row

mail.list pane: Its row holds the list's actions, and the status slot at the end: "Synced at {time}". Reading the same list again (a reload of the mailbox, a refresh, a re-read after a sync) keeps the rows already shown in place, with a thin progress bar at the top of the list while it reads, and replaces them only when the answer is in. Skeleton rows show only on a list's first read, when it has no rows to show yet, as when another mailbox or folder opens
mail.message pane: Its row sits above the subject; the subject, then From, To and Date, follow below the row as the message's content, never in it
mail.message loading: Opening a message never waits for its body, in both hosts. The message pane opens at once with what the list row already has (sender, subject, date) and a Loading message… state where the body goes. The list stays fully usable meanwhile: its rows, filters, scroll and every action answer as before. A row read from the server opens the same way: the pane at once while the message is stored. No control is disabled while a body loads; the message's own action row stays in place, empty, at its height until the message is loaded, and the Loading message… line has role=status. Opening another message, Back, or leaving the folder or the mailbox cancels the pending load (its request is aborted) and switches at once; a load that answers after it was left is never shown and never opens over what the person chose since. A load that fails says the server's reason as a sentence in the pane (the mail server could not be reached for this message; the message is not there any more; it is not this account's), with Try again there, which loads it again; never only in a notice, and nothing is tried again by itself. The one 404 also takes the message's row out of the list. A message is marked read only once it is loaded
mail.side column: Its first element (a mailbox card, or Compose) aligns its top with the rows; Compose, one control, takes pane-toolbar-height. Its left edge is the section header's content edge (the edge of the header's icon): no inset of its own. Where folders show beside the list, the side column is at least 200px wide
mail.mailbox card: One height at every width: the avatar, then the mailbox's name on one line and its address on one line, each cut with an ellipsis, the full name and address as the card's tooltip and accessible name. A count badge ("99+" above 99) is anchored to the avatar's top-right corner, the avatar being its positioning container, and never covers the name or the avatar's own letter. A mailbox's unread number is its inbox's alone; a host never sums folders, since one message counts in several of them on Gmail (the inbox, Important, All mail). The server serves it for each mailbox; until it does, a host takes the inbox's number from the folder tree (the folder whose role is inbox, else INBOX: the server's unseen once a sync has read it, else the platform's) and, from a change event, the inbox's entry in its counts, never the event's mailbox-wide unseen while that is a sum of folders. The count badge on the card's avatar is the open mailbox's own number. When another of the person's mailboxes has unread mail, a dot on the card (by its switch arrow) says so, labelled Unread mail in other mailboxes, its tooltip and accessible name. The list of mailboxes shows each mailbox's own number, and the Mail badge in the host's main navigation is the sum of the person's mailboxes' inbox numbers, each mailbox once.
mail.checked-rows bar: The list pane's row while messages are checked holds the actions on them, as the message's row does, and leads with the clear button: the cross first, then the count, "× 2 selected", and "× 2" once its label hides, by the same giving way as the other actions; its accessible name is "Clear selection (2 selected)" in the host's words
mail.folder actions: No action row over the folder column, and no actions button in a folder row: a row's actions live in its context menu, as everywhere on the platform. The menu shows the server's folder action tree (navi.toolbar.email.folder), only the nodes the host has a handler for, and opens by right-click; by a long press on touch (where hover is none or the pointer is coarse) of about 500 ms, cancelled when the finger moves to scroll, with the browser's own callout and text selection kept off the row; and by Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a focused row. New folder, the tree's list-level node, stays at the foot of the folder list. Before Delete or Empty, confirm-dialog shows the server's preview of that action as given (its title, words, count and confirm label), which says what happens to the messages, such as moving them to Trash. While Empty or Mark all as read runs on a folder (the tree's busy flag), the row shows busy and neither is offered on it; a job that fails says the server's reason in a sentence in a notice, with Retry, and the row is no longer busy; one that is done adds nothing
mail.message row actions: A message row has a context menu (context-menu), in both hosts. It shows the same action nodes as the message pane's action row, drawn the same way (groups, separators, danger, labels and icons), only the nodes the host has a handler for, and each item does exactly what the same action in the row does, with the same at-once result, notice and Undo. It opens by right-click; by a long press on touch (where hover is none or the pointer is coarse) of about 500 ms, cancelled when the finger moves to scroll, with the browser's own callout and text selection kept off the row; and by Shift+F10 or the Menu key on a focused row. Inside the menu the arrow keys move, Enter chooses and Escape closes; on close, focus returns to the row it was opened on. Selection: on a checked row the menu acts on every checked message, and its actions are those the checked-rows bar offers for them; on an unchecked row it acts on that row only and leaves the checked rows as they were (it neither checks that row nor clears the others), and it never opens the message. Which actions show, and how they are labelled (Mark read or Mark unread, Star or Remove star, Archive or not), follows the facts of what it acts on: on an unchecked row the row's own facts from its list entry, on a checked row the selection's, as the checked-rows bar reads them. Reply, Reply all and Forward from a row's menu open compose for that message without opening it in the message pane. The menu opens at the pointer for a right-click or a long press, and at the row's start, just under the row, for Shift+F10 or the Menu key; either way it is moved to stay inside the window. The browser's own menu is never replaced inside a message's body (the mail frame), in text fields, on links, or anywhere with Shift held: Shift+right-click always opens the browser's menu
mail.pane splitter: Where the grid shows more than one pane, the panes are resizable, in both hosts: one splitter between the folder column and the list, one between the list and the message. A splitter is dragged with the mouse or by touch (pointer events, the page neither scrolls nor selects text while it is dragged), and takes focus as a separator (role separator, aria-orientation vertical, aria-valuenow the pane's width in px, aria-valuemin and aria-valuemax its limits, and a name: Resize folders, Resize list). The left and right arrow keys move it by 16 px, Home and End take it to its limits, and a double-click (or Enter) puts the pane back at its default width. Widths: the folder column 230 px by default, 200 to 380 px; the list 340 px by default, 280 to 620 px; the message pane takes the rest and is never narrower than 360 px. These minimums keep the mailbox card, the list's search field and rows, and the message's header whole, and the action rows give way only as pane-toolbar says (labels, then More actions), never wrapping or clipping. A splitter never takes a pane past its limits, nor the message pane under its minimum; when the window narrows, the list gives way first and then the folder column, down to their minimums, and below what the three minimums need the grid shows fewer panes as the grid says. The widths are saved per person on the server, in the person's interface preferences (uiPrefs, written with PATCH /api/v1/auth/me/preferences as { uiPrefs: { <entry>: { columnWidths: { folders, list } } } } in px, the shape the server keeps, and read back from GET /api/v1/auth/me's uiPrefs), one entry per host, admin:mail:panes for the admin and workspace:mail:panes for the Workspace, so each keeps its own, when a drag or a key ends; local storage is only a cache, read first so the panes do not jump on load, and the server's value wins when it arrives. A width saved outside today's limits is clamped to them. No splitters where one pane shows at a time (a phone, 390 px)
mail.compose window: A message is written in a compose window, the same in both hosts. Docked: about 560 to 640 px wide (600 by default) and at most about 70% of the viewport tall, Maximize giving more, it sits at the bottom right of the window and is not modal (role dialog, aria-modal false), so the person keeps reading, selecting and copying from mail while writing; a click outside it does nothing. Its header holds the title and three buttons (Minimize, Maximize, Close), each at least 36 px; where one pane shows at a time, Minimize and Close only, each at least 44 px. Minimize turns it into a bar showing the subject (or New message) and the recipients; a click on the bar restores it, a minimized reply to the full form. Maximize makes it a large window centred over a dimmed backdrop (aria-modal true, focus kept inside), and Restore docks it again; a click on the backdrop minimizes it. Close closes the window and keeps the draft; there is no Cancel button beside it, since Close is that. Only Discard deletes a draft. Discard is always offered: with no saved draft it closes the window without saving anything; with one it deletes it (a Discard chosen while a save is still on its way waits for that save, then deletes the draft it made, so a draft never survives a Discard because the two crossed), undone within 10 seconds by the notice's Undo, as the mail actions' Undo is. Esc minimizes and keeps the draft (in the maximized state too), but an open suggestion list, menu or picker inside the window is closed by Esc first, and only the next Esc minimizes; Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac) sends. Several drafts at once: Compose always opens a new window; the open window sits at the right and minimized ones sit as bars to its left. At most 3 windows are open; opening a 4th closes the oldest, keeping its draft: the one left unused longest, never the one being written in. Where one pane shows at a time (a phone, 390 px), compose is full screen, never docked, and Minimize returns to the mail with the draft kept. The header fields are compact lines, not boxed inputs: each a row about 40 px tall with its label inside at the start and a thin divider below, the labels in one column as wide as the longest translated label (at least 52 px) so none clips or wraps; each is still a real labelled field (From a select, To, Cc and Bcc address fields). Cc and Bcc are two links at the end of the To line, each opening its own line. The editor takes the remaining height. Its contents, the same in both hosts, in this order: From, shown only when the mailbox has confirmed aliases, listing the mailbox's address and those aliases (on a reply, reply all or forward, shown read only, fixed to the mailbox of the message answered); To, with Cc and Bcc on asking, each as chips with suggestions from the person's contacts; Subject; the body in the formatting editor, whose toolbar each host builds from the editor's mail profile (profile name mail), which the mail API serves at GET /api/v1/email/editor-profile, the same for every mailbox, so it is read once and cached: { profile, contributors, allowedWidgets }, built from the same definition the server sanitises a sent message with. The server generates that profile from the definition its sanitiser keeps on send, so the editor offers nothing the server strips; a host never adds formatting of its own to it. It offers bold, italic, underline, strike, link (http, https, mailto, tel), two heading levels, bulleted and numbered lists, and quote; no images, tables, code, widgets or forms. Until that endpoint is served, both hosts use the editor's standard profile. Plain text is a checkable item in the footer's More options menu. Switching to Plain text shows the formatted body as text; switching back without editing restores the formatting exactly; after the plain text was edited, switching back first asks, since the edited text then becomes the formatted body as paragraphs and the earlier formatting is lost. What is sent is the body shown when Send is pressed; attachments from the computer and from Drive (file-picker), with the size meter against the mailbox's limit; and the footer: Send (its tooltip names Ctrl+Enter), attach (an icon), the saved state, then More options (an icon opening a menu that holds Plain text) and Discard (a trash icon, labelled Discard draft). The draft is saved automatically as it is written, on the server through its drafts API, never only in the browser, and the window says when it was saved. A reply, reply all or forward draft records what it answers (answers: { messageId, mode }), and there is at most one reply draft per person per message: reply and reply all share it (switching mode changes that same draft), the quick reply and the window share it, and it is found again by that message (the drafts API's answers lookup, the caller's own drafts only) on any device and in either host; a forward may have several drafts. A failed send for a quote or parts the server can no longer read is refused with its own problem, never sent without them. Each save carries the draft's version; a save refused as stale (409) reloads the draft and never overwrites it, and a realtime drafts event brings a change made elsewhere. The reply's threading headers are kept in the draft by the server; a host never builds reply headers in the browser. The draft is deleted only after a send has succeeded, by sending with its draftId; a failed send keeps it. Reply, Reply all and Forward (from the action row, a row's menu or the checked-rows bar) always open this window, prefilled from the server's compose prefill for that message and mode (GET /api/v1/email/messages/{id}/compose?mode=reply, reply_all or forward): From, To, Cc and Bcc, Subject, and the editor empty and focused. The quote is never in the editor: the server appends it when the message is sent. Below the editor the quote is collapsed by default behind a ••• button (labelled Show the quoted message, aria-expanded), with Remove quote beside it. Opened, the window shows the prefill's quote.html read only in a framed box under its attribution line, at most about 320 px tall and scrolling inside, drawn in the sandboxed mail frame under the mail frame page's rules (quote.text in Plain text, as a read-only preview only: in Plain text the server itself appends the quote as "> " lines), with Remove quote, after which the message is sent without it and the quote is no longer shown. A host always sends the quote choice explicitly (quote true or false), since the server's defaults differ: off for a reply, on for a forward. A quote the server can no longer read refuses the send (quoted-message-unavailable), nothing is sent, and the window says so and offers to send without the quote. A quick reply's Expand, or Reply while a quick reply holds text, opens this window for that message with the quick reply's text and attachments moved into it: one draft, never two
mail.server rows: A folder the platform has not fully synced (every folder but the inbox, until its sync is complete) lists the mail server's messages in the same list, in both hosts: the list answer holds rows marked fromServer, with no id and a ref, beside the folder's own stored rows, in one order, the server's newest first. A host shows a server row like any other row, keyed by its ref, and never sorts or merges rows itself. The list pages by the cursor the answer gives (the X-Next-Cursor header), reading the next page as the person scrolls; a cursor refused as stale (409) starts the list again from the top, keeping nothing of the old pages. A server row offers Open only: it has no checkbox, the row menu and the checked-rows bar leave it out, and none of the message actions is offered on it. Opening it (selecting it) stores it through the server-message opener, then opens the stored message by its id in the message pane; the opener marks nothing read, so the host then marks it read as on any open (its usual seen request); the row is then an ordinary row with every action. A ref the server answers as gone says the message is no longer on the mail server and takes the row out. A realtime change reads the first page again and leaves the rows of later pages as they are. When the answer says the mail server could not be reached (X-Server-Pages: unavailable), on any page, the rows already shown stay, and a line at the list's end says older messages could not be loaded, with Try again; a page refused as too many requests says how long to wait and offers Try again after it. A folder listed this way never shows the Older on the mail server section, which belongs to the inbox only. The folder's total and unread counts are the server's counts the folder tree gives; a host never counts the rows it shows
mail.quick reply: A short, chat-like box pinned at the bottom of the message pane, outside the message's scroll region, in both hosts, for the open message. Collapsed it is one line: an attach button (icon), the field reading Reply to <name>... (the sender it goes to), Expand (icon) and Send; Send is muted until there is text. As text is typed the field grows with the text to about 6 lines, then scrolls inside itself. The file chips and the size meter show above the line only once files are attached. It has no To, Cc or Subject: it goes to the sender (the message's Reply-To when it has one) with Re: on the subject, as the server's reply prefill gives them. It holds plain text and attachments (the same attach as the compose window, with its size meter). Ctrl+Enter (Cmd+Enter on a Mac) sends; Enter is a new line. The server appends the quote on send (the box sends quote true); the quote is not shown in the box, and sending without it takes the compose window (Remove quote). What is typed is that message's reply draft on the server (the one draft per person per message the compose window also uses), autosaved after a pause, so it survives opening another message, a reload, another device and the other host; Expand hands the same draft to the window, so there is never a second one. Expand, or Reply while the box holds text, moves the text and attachments into the compose window (one draft), and the box gives way to the line "Your reply is open in the compose window." with Show it, which restores and focuses that window. Each host says where a draft is written on every create and save (composedIn: quick-reply from the box, window from the compose window); the server keeps window once said and reads a draft that never said as window, so after a reload or on another device a reply draft marked window shows as the Draft line, never in the box. Once that draft has gone to the compose window it never comes back into the box: the window may hold changed recipients, Cc, a new subject, a removed quote or formatting the box cannot show, so a send from the box could go where the person does not expect. When the window is closed and the draft kept, the line shows the start of the draft (Draft: and its first words) with Open, which opens the compose window on it, and Discard, which deletes it at once with the same 10 s Undo as the window's Discard. Once the reply is sent or the draft discarded, the line goes back to the empty box. After a send the box clears and the notice says it was sent. A server row (not yet opened) has no quick reply. On a phone the box stays pinned at the bottom of the message, and Expand opens the compose window full screen
mail.spam: A message whose own folder is the mailbox's spam folder (the folder with the junk role, whatever its name) keeps its remote content blocked, in both hosts, by that folder and never by the list it was opened from: from a folder's list, a search (local or on the server), a conversation, the next message after an action, or an address alike: Load images is not offered and the Load images variant of the mail frame page is never used for it, whatever the person's setting for remote images; its links are not followable (drawn as text, not as links, so a click opens nothing); and a warning above the message says it was marked as spam and that its images and links are blocked for that reason. The server's sanitiser does its part for such a message; the host never relies on it alone. The blocks lift only when the message's own folder changes away from the spam folder: Not spam, Move, or a move made in another client and heard in real time
mail.drafts view: The Drafts folder lists every draft of the mailbox, in both hosts: the drafts written here, which open in the compose window and stay editable, and the drafts on the mail server that another mail app wrote, listed from the server, which are read-only. A host tells them apart by the list alone: in the folder whose role is drafts, a row marked fromServer (a server row, with a ref and no id) is another app's draft. The drafts written here are no row of the folder's list at all (the server leaves the person's own drafts out of it, stored or from the server): a host lists them from the drafts API (GET /api/v1/email/mailboxes/{mailboxId}/drafts/list) beside the folder's list and opens them in the compose window from there, so none is listed twice. A draft from another app is marked as from another app in its row, opens in the message pane as a message does, through the server-message opener as any server row (never in the compose window), and offers no edit, send or discard; the person writes it in the app that made it
mail.grid: At breakpoint-desktop and above, the mail grid fills the viewport below the page's section header, with the page's own spacing between the header and the grid kept; the page itself never scrolls. Each pane's action row stays put, and so does the list's search field; under them, each pane has exactly one scroll region. The same rule holds wherever two panes show side by side, and inside the one pane where one shows at a time
mail.message pane scroll: The message pane scrolls once: the message's header (subject, From, To, Date), its body and its raw source move together in one scroll region under the action row. The frame the mail is drawn in grows to its content's height and never scrolls itself. The frame is the mail frame page described below, and the host measures its document from outside (its scroll height, again as it changes); no script ever runs in the frame, and nothing about the frame is weakened to measure it. The quick reply is not in this scroll region: it is pinned below it, at the bottom of the message pane (see quick reply). The frame's height is computed again after remote images load and whenever the pane's width changes. Until Show original is served in both hosts, the raw source sits at the true end of the message with no scroll of its own (long lines scroll sideways at most)
mail.mail frame page: A message is drawn in a frame whose document is a page of the host's own, served from the host's origin (never srcdoc, which takes the host page's policy and breaks the mail under a strict one). The host puts the server-sanitised HTML into that document and measures it from outside; the server's sanitising stays the first control and this page is the second. The frame's sandbox is exactly allow-same-origin allow-popups allow-popups-to-escape-sandbox, never allow-scripts. The page is served with Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and with exactly this Content-Security-Policy, the same text in both hosts: "default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data:; font-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'". A second variant of the page, used only after the person chooses Load images for that message, serves exactly "default-src 'none'; script-src 'none'; object-src 'none'; frame-src 'none'; form-action 'none'; base-uri 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: https:; font-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'self'". No font from a message ever loads, remote or data:, not even after Load images: font-src is 'none' in both variants, and the server's sanitising drops external stylesheets and every @font-face rule. style-src 'unsafe-inline' is allowed on this page only, never on a host page. The message's own parts (inline images) are fetched through the host's URL (img-src 'self'). Each host has a test that its frame page answers with exactly this policy text, in both variants, and both headers. Before the HTML goes in, the host sets rel="noopener noreferrer" on every a[href] and area[href], whatever came with it. The page carries <base target="_blank"> and never a base address (base-uri 'none' refuses an href; a target alone is allowed). The host measures the document from outside without observing the size of anything inside it, which a browser reports as a resize loop: a ResizeObserver on the frame element for its width, a MutationObserver on its document, and a capture-phase load and error listener for images, each scheduling one fit on the next animation frame that writes the height only when it changes by at least 1px
mail.show original: The message's source is not shown in the reading pane: "Show original" is the server's action node (menu only, overflow 0) and opens a full-screen viewer with one scroll region. It shows the source as escaped plain text only: no HTML, no links made from text, no images; bytes that are not valid UTF-8 shown as the replacement character. At most the first 1 MB is shown, with "Showing the first 1 MB; download for the full source" when there is more. Copy copies what is shown; Download saves the whole message as .eml from the server. Its keys and focus are the file-viewer's. The inline raw source leaves the pane once both hosts render Show original
mail.after archive or delete: After Archive, Delete or Move takes the open message out of the list as it shows (decided before the server answers: the message stays shown when the list shown holds every message, the all-mail role, and the action is a move into a label or Archive; otherwise it leaves; when it stays shown, it stays open), where the list and the message show side by side, the message pane opens the next message: the one that took the removed message's place in the list, or the one above it when it was the last; it is marked read by the same rule as any message opened. Where one pane shows at a time, the list shows again. After an action on checked messages, when the message open was one of them, the nearest message not checked opens, the one below first; when none is left, the message pane is empty. Which message opens is the host's, from the list as it shows it; the server is not asked. A per-person choice of what follows is not part of this entry
mail.read state: A message is marked read only by being opened: the person selecting it (or the next message opening after an action, by the rule above). Never by a render again, a refresh of the list, a realtime event, or an update of the shared record of the message. After Mark read or Mark unread, the message shows the state the person chose at once, and nothing read or sent before the server answered that action changes it: a list read started before the answer, or an event older than the answer. The answer carries the server's sequence for the message (the mail API names the field), and an event for that message with a lower sequence is dropped. When two read actions are in flight for one message, the one the person chose last wins, and the earlier one's answer applies nothing. After the answer, the server is right: an event for that message saying the opposite of what the person chose means the change was refused, and the host says so in a notice, with the server's reason when the event gives one, replacing any notice of success; it never reverts silently. A refusal that comes after the server first accepted the change (a later rollback, announced by its own refusal event with a reason) is said exactly as one refused at once: the same notice, in the same words, such as "Couldn't mark as unread: " followed by the server's sentence for the reason, as given. The state then stays as the server has it until the person opens the message or chooses again
mail.at once: A mail action shows its result the moment it is chosen, before the server answers. Archive, Delete and Move take the message out of the list at once, and the next message opens by the rule above; Mark read or unread and Star change the row and the open message at once. A notice says what was done, in the host's words, such as "Moved to Trash" or "Archived". When the server refuses, the message comes back to its place in the list, and its row's state as it was; it opens again only when it was open and the message that opened after it is still shown untouched (not read on to, acted on or left). Otherwise the person stays where they are. The refusal's notice replaces the notice of what was done, never adding a second, and says why with the server's detail as given (the state component's rule on whose words). Nothing is retried by itself. One state for a message on every surface: the toolbar, the row's menu and the checked-rows bar read the same record, so an action shown on one is shown on the others. The notice of a move, a delete to Trash or an archive carries Undo once the server's answer brings its undo token (the token's field and the undo endpoint are the mail API's), never for a refused action; it lasts 10 seconds from then or until the next mail action, whichever comes first, and the 10 seconds stop while the notice has focus or the pointer is over it; Undo posts the server's undo token from that action's answer and puts back what the server reports put back, each message to its place in the list; a message moved since gets its own sentence, and a refusal its reason. Undo is never offered for Empty, a delete from Trash or a folder delete
mail.list scrolling: The message list, and a search's results (the platform's and More on the server alike), load more as the person scrolls, in both hosts, with no Load more button and no setting for it. The next page is asked for when about one and a half screens of rows remain below what is shown (by the cursor the answer gives: one cursor for every folder, running through the stored rows and on into the mail server's for a folder not fully synced, so new mail never shifts it; until every folder gives one, by the next page number where none is given; the last page gives none), and a Loading... row stands at the list's end while it reads. A page that fails turns that row into Couldn't load, with Retry; a page refused as too many requests turns it into Retry in N s, counting down from Retry-After, then Retry. That row is the only place a retry is offered: the earlier Load older from the server button survives only as it, and the inbox's separate Older on the mail server section goes into the same scrolling once the one cursor is served. The list is virtualized: only the rows in view and a small buffer above and below are in the page, so a folder of thousands of messages scrolls as lightly as a short one, and keyboard focus and the open message's row are kept when they scroll out of view. Each row carries aria-posinset (its place in the list) and aria-setsize (the folder's total from the folder tree, or -1 while it is not known), so a screen reader says where it is. New mail heard in real time never moves what the person is looking at: when they are scrolled down, a New messages: N pill at the top of the list says how many came, and a click on it scrolls to the top, where they are; at the top, they simply appear. Select all checks the rows loaded so far, and says so (for example 150 selected); selecting every message of a folder for one action on the server is not offered
mail.folder icons: Every row of the folder list carries an icon before its name, in both hosts, chosen by the folder's role from the folder tree, never by its name, and drawn the size of the row's text in its color. The icons are Bootstrap Icons names, each kit mapping them by its one table, as the pane toolbar's are: inbox inbox; sent send; drafts file-earmark-text; archive and all archive; trash trash; flagged star; important bookmark; junk exclamation-octagon; and any other folder, including one that only holds folders, folder. A role the host does not know draws folder. The icon is decorative (aria-hidden): the row's name is its label.
mail.folder rows: A row of the folder list keeps one height at every width of the folder column, in both hosts. Its icon, its unread badge and its total never shrink and never wrap: a badge is always as wide as its text plus its padding. Only the folder's name gives way: one line, cut with an ellipsis, the full name in the row's tooltip, and the row's accessible name is always the full name. A row shows one total beside the unread badge: the server's count of the folder's messages once a sync has read it, otherwise the platform's own count, as the unread badge chooses its number; a folder that only holds folders shows no total. While the platform has not yet stored the whole folder, and only when both numbers are known and differ, how much it has (for example 3,688 of 4,044 stored) is said in the row's tooltip or the mailbox's sync line, never as a second number in the row. The folder column is never narrower than its content needs, measured over every folder of the mailbox, shown or collapsed: the widest row's indent, icon, badge and total plus 6ch of name, or 200px, whichever is larger. The splitter beside it stops there; a saved width below it is shown at the minimum, and written back only when the person moves the splitter.
mail.attachment view: A message's attachment is viewed in the app only as the server says, in both hosts: each row of the message's attachments carries viewAs, pdf, image or none, which the server decides from the file's first bytes against an allowlist (PDF, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), never from its declared type or its name; SVG and HTML are never viewed. A host offers View only for pdf and image, and chooses the viewer only from viewAs, so a PDF sent as application/octet-stream still opens and a file named .pdf that is not one does not. Until viewAs is served, a host offers View only for a declared application/pdf or a declared PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, never SVG; once it is served it replaces the declared type completely, and viewAs none means no View, with no fallback. Every attachment keeps Download and Save to Drive. A pdf opens in the app's PDF viewer, with nothing in the document run (no scripts, no XFA, no eval); an image opens in a preview over the page, made from the downloaded bytes under the type the download serves (the detected safe type, sent with nosniff), and Esc closes it. The viewer's label shows the detected kind (PDF, or the image's kind), while the attachment's line in the message keeps its declared type. An attachment is never opened in a new tab or as a page of the app's own origin. The shared file-viewer replaces both once it is built

host.supplies: the server's action nodes for the pane, only those it has a handler for; a handler for each; the server's sentence for a disabled one, as the node gives it; which are busy; the status text, formatted; the toolbar's label and moreLabel; the question before an action that cannot be undone, through confirm-dialog
host.left to it: what each action does; how it maps the server's nodes to actions, carrying only what a node gives (a node with no group is in the one group, in the tree's order; with no overflow number it never goes behind More actions); the row's inline padding, its background and the edge below it; navigation that is not an action on the pane's object, such as Back where one pane shows at a time, which leads the row when it shares it, before the first group, and never goes behind More actions; and the side column's first element itself

pane-toolbar.notes: pane-toolbar-height is the row's height and the side column's first element's: a control (row-height) with space-2 above and below it. The actions are the server's NaviGraph nodes, not this entry's. First built by the mail screens of the admin and the Workspace; a kit declares this entry once it provides the row. No release of this contract until ui-react and ui-angular both implement it, as with file-picker.

notification.purpose: One notification in the person's notification list (the bell): its title, its body, and an optional action that takes the person where the notification is about.

parts.body: The title is the row's extras.title and the text its extras.body. A host draws both as plain text, always, whatever extras.bodyFormat says (a markdown or dtmpl body from a manual send shows its source text; the server renders neither), and never makes them, or the row, a link of its own; only an action with presentation row makes the row open something. The chevron only expands and collapses the body; it never navigates.
parts.action: A notification may carry an action: { label, labelText, destination: { name, params }, presentation }, or none. presentation is button (the default when absent) or row, and the server decides it, never the host. label is a code (such as reconnect or manage-access) that the host translates into its own words; labelText is the server's fallback text, shown when the host has no translation for that code. destination.name is a name from the server's registered list, never a URL, and params is a flat map of the values its route needs (such as mailboxId, and an optional section). Each host maps the names it knows, with their params, to its own routes. With presentation button, a known destination with its required params shows an explicit button under the text, labelled as above, and pressing it goes to the host's route. With presentation row, no button is shown: the whole row is the action, a real interactive element named by the label (as above) that opens the destination on a click, a tap or Enter, as for a missed call or a mention, whose destination is chat.conversation. A notification has at most one row action. A name the host does not know, or a required param missing, shows no button and gives the row no destination: the row navigates nowhere, and nothing else about the notification changes. A host never decides navigation by the notification's type: with no destination, or one it does not know, nothing navigates. The action grants nothing: the screen it opens checks the person's rights itself. A row may instead carry a link (other kinds of notification use it); a row the server sends carries one or the other, and if one ever carries both, the action is the button.

notification.behaviour: The same in both hosts. Pressing a notification's row (a click, a tap, or Enter on it) marks it read, whatever it carries; it navigates only when its action's presentation is row and the host knows the destination, and a button action navigates only from its button, which marks it read too. So a notification with no action, or one whose destination the host does not know, can still be read, and the unread count goes down by reading as well as by dismissing. Expanding the body with the chevron also marks it read. The button is a real button, in the notification's tab order after its text, named by its label. A notification may be updated in place by the server (the same id with a new title, body, extras and createdAt, as missed calls from one conversation are grouped into one while it is unread): a host replaces that row where it is and never adds a second one, places it again by createdAt (the list stays newest first, so it moves to the top), and counts it once among the unread. A host draws the server's title and body; extras such as count and times are there for a host that wants its own words. A notification shown outside the app (a phone's or a browser's) uses the notification's id as its collapse key or tag, so it too is replaced, never repeated.
notification.notes: The action is served with the notification type registry's amendment; until a host reads it, a row shows no button. First built by the admin's notification drawer and the Workspace's notification list. No release of this contract until ui-react and ui-angular both implement it, as with the other entries.

settings-shell.purpose: The layout every settings-like page shares: a list of sections on the left, the chosen section on the right. The admin's Settings and My Profile, and any page whose content is a set of named sections, one shown at a time.

parts.list: The sections, in the order the page's declared tree gives them, grouped where it groups them; each a row with its label (and icon where the tree gives one), the chosen one marked (aria-current), a danger section in the danger colour. The page passes the sections; the layout never chooses what is listed.
parts.head: Optional, above the list, in the list's column: what the page shows of its subject whatever section is open (My Profile's avatar, colour and name card). It scrolls with the list.
parts.section: The chosen section, its own title at its top, its content below. Choosing another section changes the section and the address only.
parts.phone: Below the tablet breakpoint the list and the section are not side by side: the list (with its head) is the screen; choosing a section shows it in the list's place, with a Back to the list. The address names the section, so a section can be opened directly.

settings-shell.empty: No section is listed: the list says so in the page's words, and the section's place draws the empty pane (state, kind empty). Sections listed and none chosen yet: from tablet width up the first section opens, so the section's place is never blank; at phone width the list is the screen until one is chosen.
settings-shell.notes: From tablet width up the list's column is resizable (the pane splitter), between about 200 and 440px. A page with sections from a declared tree takes their labels, icons, order and conditions from it, and adds none of its own.

screen-shell.purpose: One screen of a section at phone width, one pane at a time: one top bar, optional filter chips, the content, an optional floating primary action, and the section bar below. The same in every section and every host, so moving between sections never changes where things are. What goes in its slots (the title, where Back leads, the primary action, the filters, the section's search) is the host's, from the server's declared nodes; the shell only lays them out.

parts.bar: One row, --cms-topbar-height, never wrapping: leading, title and trailing, centred vertically. The only header of the screen: no second Back row or title in the content, at any depth.
parts.leading: At a section's root: the section's own navigation (mail's folders) as an icon button, or nothing. On a nested screen: Back, an icon button with the parent's name beside it, the name truncated first, leading to the parent.
parts.title: The current place's name (the folder, the conversation, the drive folder): --cms-font-size-title-md, one line, truncated, its whole text as its title.
parts.trailing: In this order: the section's search (an icon button), then the shell's own icons: the bell with its count on its corner, and the person's avatar, which carries the live connection (avatar, connection); no separate connection dot. Every icon one style: --cms-control-height-md square, no box, --cms-text-muted, the hover background.
parts.search: While the section's search is open (searching): Close, an icon button, leading, then the host's search field filling the rest of the bar; the title and the icons give way. The bar keeps its height. Close, or the host, ends it. Search opens in place, never as a screen of its own.
parts.filters: Optional, under the bar: the place's filters as chips in one row that scrolls sideways, exactly one selected; a second fixed row.
parts.content: The rest of the height, scrolling on its own; a list is drawn with list's row anatomy.
parts.primary: Optional: one floating button, bottom right, --cms-space-4 from the content's edges, above the section bar: a circle of --cms-control-height-lg plus --cms-space-3, the primary colour, --cms-shadow-md, its icon at 24px, its label as its accessible name and tooltip. The content ends with room for it, so its last row scrolls clear. Not shown on an item's own screen (a message, a conversation, a file). While drafts are minimized to bars above the section bar, it stands above them. It may open a menu instead of running one action (with-primary-menu): drive's + lists its own entries first (Upload, New folder), then the create entries installed modules contribute (new document, spreadsheet, image), all from the declared tree, none listed in a kit or a host.
parts.pull: A list refreshes by a pull from its top: a pull past 64px shows the refresh state and calls the host. There is no refresh button in the bar. The time of the last sync, when the host has one, is said while pulled.

api.title: string
api.back: optional { label: the parent's name, href or onBack }; absent at a root
api.navigation: optional: the root's leading element, an icon button the host supplies
api.filters: optional { options: { id, label }[], selected, onSelect }
api.primary: optional { label, icon, onPress } or { label, icon, menu }; given only when the server declares the action (mail's compose, chat's new conversation, drive's create entries)
api.onRefresh: optional: () => Promise; with it the content takes the pull
api.pullText: optional: what the pull says, the sync time
api.searching: optional { field: the host's search field, closeLabel, onClose }; while given, the bar is in its searching state
api.barHidden: optional boolean, the kit's own when not given: the bar steps out of view while the content scrolls down and comes back on any scroll up, at the content's top, or when focus moves into the bar

behaviour: Phone width only, below --cms-breakpoint-tablet. Wider, a section's panes keep their own rows (pane-toolbar) and the shell is not drawn.
Back on a nested screen and the browser's or the system's back lead to the same parent.
The bar never reflows the content: its height is fixed, and filters, when present, are a second fixed row.
The bell and the avatar are the shell's, not the section's: the same in every section, in the same place.

bar-hidden: while the content scrolls down, the bar (and the filters row under it) steps out of view, so the content has the screen; any scroll up, reaching the content's top, or focus moving into the bar brings it back at once. The section bar below stays. Never while searching, pulling or refreshing.

One header at phone width: while a screen shell is drawn, the host's own top bar gives way, and what it carried for the whole host (the account, the host's search) is handed to the shell's bar (trailing, search). The kit's app shell does this itself when a screen shell is mounted in it, not by a host's CSS.

host.supplies: the title and the back target, both declared nodes: /title, its label the section's root title, and /back, its meta.target section or parent, absent at a root. Back is drawn with the parent's name from the data, the node's label as the fallback. Also the root navigation, the section's search, the filters, the primary action or menu when declared, and the refresh call
host.left to it: what search, the primary action and refresh do; the section's content

screen-shell.notes: First built for the workspace's mail, chat and drive, web and app. The slots' content comes from NaviGraph trees: mail's navi.toolbar.email.*, drive's navi.toolbar.drive.folder (its create entries contributed per installed kind), chat's navi.toolbar.chat.list and navi.toolbar.chat.conversation. The drive and chat trees are the ones agreed with the server; a host draws a slot only from a tree the server serves. The shell carries no list of actions of its own. A kit with no phone sections (the admin) declares it not offered, with its reason.

conventions: Dates and times, in every component: formatted in the interface language the person chose, never the browser's.
